atoms.text:
Nuclear power plants produce about 15% of the electricity in the UK. They use a very different source of energy from fossil fuels. But where does this energy come from?

Everything around us is made up of very small pieces of matter called atoms. At the center of each atom is a nucleus. Nuclear power plants use the energy that is released when nuclei split, in a process called nuclear fission. That’s where the name nuclear power comes from.

Nuclear fission creates heat, which is used to turn water into steam. This steam turns turbines and generators, which produce electricity.

instruction.text: Decide whether the statement is an advantage or disadvantage of nuclear power.

atoms.a: The fuel is very efficient. Nuclear fuel can produce millions of times more energy than the same quantity of coal.
Nuclear reactors do not produce greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide.

Nuclear power plants produce radioactive waste, which continues to release deadly radiation for many years. Nuclear radiation is harmful to the environment and can damage the human body by destroying cells. It is very difficult to store this waste safely.

Modern nuclear reactors are designed to be very safe. However, a nuclear accident can put people and the environment in danger. This happened at a nuclear power plant in Fukushima, Japan, in 2011. An earthquake and tsunami caused damage, allowing radioactive material to escape. People living nearby were forced to leave their homes.
